parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State what is meant by work done.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
A diver releases a solid sphere of radius $16\text{ cm}$ from the sea bed. The sphere moves vertically upwards towards the surface of the sea.

The weight of the sphere is $20\text{ N}$. The upthrust acting on the sphere is $170\text{ N}$. The upthrust remains constant as the sphere moves upwards.
parts.text: Calculate the density of the material of the sphere.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Briefly explain the origin of the upthrust acting on the sphere.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Calculate the acceleration of the sphere as it is released from rest.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text:
The viscous (drag) force $D$ acting on the sphere is given by

$$D = kr^2v^2$$

where $r$ is the radius of the sphere and $v$ is its speed. The constant $k$ is equal to $810\text{ kg m}^{-3}$.

Determine the constant (terminal) speed reached by the sphere.

parts.label: (b)(v)
parts.text:
The diver releases a different sphere that moves with a constant speed of $6.30\text{ m s}^{-1}$ directly towards a stationary ship. The sphere emits sound of frequency $4850\text{ Hz}$. The ship detects sound of frequency $4870\text{ Hz}$ as the sphere moves towards it.

Determine, to three significant figures, the speed of the sound in the water.
